metadata.title: Example Fleet Readiness Analytics Service Plan of Action and Milestones (draft)

observations.title: ac-2 determination
observations.description: Examined access requests and approvals for a random sample across the five roles, the 2026-10-06 quarterly review record, the 35-day inactivity setting and the role-change events; re-ran six DT-2 sign-in and inactivity cases (pass); interviewed the ISSO. Account types, approvals, provisioning through broker groups, monitoring and the quarterly review are in place. The leaver-timing test (PRC-004, 2026-12-01) of ten leavers found no evidence that any departure reached the account manager within the 24 hours the SSP sets: the two known leavers were removed only at the quarterly review, and the other eight checklists record no notification time (ASM-020). Account management is not aligned with the termination and transfer processes. Pre-production accounts only.

observations.title: au-11 determination
observations.description: Examined the retention settings of the three log stores and queried each for its oldest record: each holds 90 days, against the one-year retention the tailored control sets. The CSSP's one-year copy is kept under the CSSP's own schedule, retrievable only by ticket and changeable without the program's agreement, so it does not meet the program's retention duty. Interviewed the ISSO and the CSSP liaison. The SSP records the control as partial, with an archive tier in release 1.6.

observations.title: ca-2 determination
observations.description: Examined sap.yaml and ART-SAP: the AODR selected an independent team on 2026-11-18 and approved the plan, which names the 50 controls, 17 procedures, the pre-production environment, the team and the roles, on 2026-11-18, before the assessment started on 2026-11-19. Interviewed the ISSM. This assessment is the first; no assessment report has yet been produced or delivered, and the recurring annual assessment of a third of the controls is written into ART-CONMON but not yet scheduled. The SSP statement for ca-2 predates A-1 and A-2 and still says no assessor is selected (left to A-5).

observations.title: ca-3 determination
observations.description: Examined the supply status service agreement (2026-06-30) and the identity broker onboarding approval (2026-05-12), both signed and documenting interface, security and privacy requirements, responsibilities and impact level; examined the EMIS ISSM's interim e-mail approval of 2026-09-15, which names only the interface; tested the EFRAS end of each exchange (mutual TLS and signature check on the EMIS extract, read-only API pull, SAML assertion validation), all as designed. Interviewed the PM. The EMIS exchange, which carries maintainer PII, is not approved and managed by an agreement: the memorandum of agreement is unsigned (target 2026-12-31).

observations.title: ca-5 determination
observations.description: Examined the eMASS POA&M module (empty) and the program backlog tickets for the seven known limitations; interviewed the ISSM and the PM. No plan of action and milestones exists yet; the known weaknesses are tracked only as backlog tickets with fix releases. The SSP records ca-5 as planned, to be met at A-6. M-2 2027-02-01 (ca-5 monthly): still other-than-satisfied. Examined artifacts/poam/items.yaml: the plan now exists for every open finding, with milestones, resources and the AO's review of 2027-01-25 (CA-05a in substance). Its eMASS entry and its one monthly update of 2027-01-15 are milestone records made under the R-3 progress rule (ASM-025), not records the assessor can examine, and one update cannot show the monthly cadence the tailored ca-5 sets (CA-05b). The ISSO confirms the update cadence has not yet produced a monthly roll-up. FND-005 stays open until its own milestone, the assessor's verification of the plan and its update history by 2027-03-31.

observations.title: ca-7 determination
observations.description: Examined ART-CONMON, approved by the AODR on 2026-11-18 with its metrics and frequencies, and the pre-production monitoring records: weekly scans and log reviews, hourly drift reports, the 2026-10-06 account review, the CSSP's correlation tickets and the backlog tickets they raised. Interviewed the ISSM and the PM. No ongoing control assessment has run and no security or privacy status report (monthly roll-up, quarterly posture report) has been produced under the strategy; the SSP records ca-7 as planned until the first cycle after authorization. M-2 2027-02-01 (ca-7 monthly): still other-than-satisfied. This first ongoing assessment is itself the start of CA-07c. But the monitoring records that reached the assessor end on 2026-11-15, ten weeks before the authorization of 2027-01-25, and cover the pre-production account only; no monthly roll-up has been compiled, nothing for December or January went to the PM, the ISSM or the AODR, and no posture report exists yet (CA-07g). Monitoring did run in that fortnight as the strategy says: drift, image and node scans, log and alert review, an account spot check, the privacy record and threat updates. The measures are outside their limits (MRS-01, MRS-02 in conmon.yaml). FND-006 stays open.

observations.title: cm-3 determination
observations.description: A-3: examined a random sample of 8 of the 23 pull requests merged between releases 1.5.0 and 1.5.1 (each with a second reviewer, a security and privacy impact note, green gates and an ISSE or ISSO sign-off; no emergency change), the CCB minutes of 2026-09 to 2026-11, and the retention of repository and pipeline records; tested that a direct change to the cluster outside the pipeline is reported by the drift scan within the hour; interviewed the ISSE; satisfied. M-2 2027-02-01 (data to 2026-11-15): other-than-satisfied. The drift record shows a configuration-controlled change made on 2026-11-04 from the provider console, outside the pull request, gate and board path, with no emergency change raised: a security group was widened during troubleshooting and was neither reviewed nor approved before it was made. The engineers' console role can still write security groups in both accounts (ISSO). Monitoring of change activity (CM-03f) worked, since the drift scan flagged and the pipeline reverted the change within the hour. Release 1.6 (CHG-003) went through review, test and board approval with its impact analysis. Examined the cycle's drift record and the change log; interviewed the ISSO.

observations.title: cm-6 determination
observations.description: Reused RR-001 and ran the SCA's authenticated scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23 over the nodes, the images and the database instance: same result as 2026-10-22, nodes 94% with only provider-managed control plane checks open, database with STG-001 and STG-002 open (program-fixable, release 1.5.2 not yet in pre-production) and STG-003 to STG-006 recorded as the provider's settings under LA-01; no CAT I. Examined ART-STIG and stig-summary.yaml, the drift reports and the change records. The Application Security and Development STIG review of INV-002 to INV-006 (BM-04, 2026-11-24) found no documented secure configuration for the five containers to review against (ASM-021). Interviewed the ISSE and the developer. M-2 2027-02-01 (data to 2026-11-15): not reassessed, result kept. No SCAP STIG scan after 2026-11-23 and no container checklist result reached the assessor; release 1.6 (CHG-003) is said to carry the STG-001 setting and the container baseline check, but nothing the assessor can examine or rescan shows them in place, so FND-007 and FND-008 stay open for the verification COND-05 requires by 2027-03-31.

observations.title: cm-8 determination
observations.description: Compared 20 deployed resources (nodes, images, database, buckets, keys) with the INV list: every one is listed, none twice, none belonging to another system, with the fields the SSP names. The inventory still records the five containers at 1.5.0 while release 1.5.1 has run in the assessed environment since 2026-11-07, and no review at that release is recorded, although the SSP sets review at every release. Interviewed the ISSE. M-2 2027-02-01: result kept. The inventory now records release 1.6 and which environment runs what, but the record was updated on 2027-02-01, seventeen days after the release of 2027-01-15, with no review dated at the release, and no production deployment is recorded to confirm it against; FND-009 stays open.

observations.title: cp-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the whole of the contingency plan, version 1.0 draft (ART-CP), against the control: it covers the essential function, the 24-hour objectives, restoration order and metrics, roles with the on-call roster, continued reporting from EMIS during an outage, restoration from the templates, coordination with incident handling through the CSSP ticket path, and repository protection. It has not been reviewed or approved by the PM, has not been distributed to the key personnel or to EMIS and the CSSP, has had no annual review, and no change to it has been communicated. Interviewed the ISSE. The SSP records cp-2 as partial; the S-6 approval asks the PM to approve it by 2026-12-15.

observations.title: cp-4 determination
observations.description: Examined the plan and every test record: the only test is the DT-2 database point-in-time restore (3 h 10 min). Re-performed that restore on 2026-12-02 in pre-production: it finished well inside the 24-hour objective and the ISSE reviewed the result; no corrective action was needed. No regional failover of the cluster and no tabletop exercise has been held (planned 2027-02), so the plan's effectiveness and the readiness to execute it are not tested as the tailored control sets (annual tabletop, restore and failover tests). Interviewed the ISSE.

observations.title: ia-2 determination
observations.description: Tested CAC sign-in through the broker for all five roles and the six console roles (re-performing DT-2), and traced the DoD ID number from the assertion to the session and to every audit event of the test (uniquely tied); refused a sign-in without an approved group. Examined the two break-glass console accounts: they authenticate with FIDO2 keys, not CAC, and a use is tied to a person only by the two-person seal log and the alert; neither has been used. The deviation from the DoD CAC requirement has not been put to the AO. Interviewed the ISSO. The SSP records ia-2 as partial for this reason.

observations.title: ia-5 determination
observations.description: Examined the FIDO2 key issue record (in person against ID, defaults changed at issue), the key service inventory (no long-lived access keys; program keys rotated 2026-03-02), the break-glass database password change record (2026-07-01, inside 180 days) and the seal log; tested that a workload token expires with its session. The local break-glass database role's password complexity falls short of the PostgreSQL STIG rule on both the 2026-10-22 scan and the SCA's 2026-11-23 scan (STG-002, CAT II, fix in release 1.5.2). Interviewed the ISSO.

observations.title: ir-4 determination
observations.description: Examined the operations runbook, the on-call roster, the CSSP service agreement and its handling playbook evidence (the October service report, the DoD O-8530.01-M evaluation), and the draft incident response plan (ART-IRP); walked the handling steps through with the ISSO and the CSSP liaison. Detection and analysis (CSSP, confirmed against its package, EXT-004), containment, eradication and recovery (runbook steps; the restore re-performed under cp-4) are in place, and the CSSP applies one playbook to every system it serves. The capability is not yet consistent with an incident response plan, because ART-IRP is an unapproved draft nobody is trained on; coordination with contingency planning exists only between two unapproved, unexercised drafts; and no lessons-learned step has run. The SSP records ir-4 as partial.

observations.title: ir-8 determination
observations.description: Examined ART-IRP and incident-response.yaml against every part of the control: the plan gives the roadmap, structure and fit within the Component and the CSSP service, defines reportable incidents and categories, sets metrics (time to report, time to contain, after-action items closed), names resources and management support, covers sharing of incident information and designates the ISSO, the on-call engineers and the CSSP. It has not been reviewed or approved (the PM approves by 2026-12-15), has not been distributed to the incident response personnel or to the CSSP and the privacy office, and no change has been communicated. It is kept in the repository with access limited to its holders. Interviewed the ISSM. The SSP records ir-8 as planned.

observations.title: pl-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the whole plan set (ART-SSP, the per-family statements, ART-CMP, ART-CP, ART-IRP, ART-CONMON and the privacy plan content) against each part of the control, with the S-6 approval record and the I-2 update (version 1.1, 2026-11-18). The plans are consistent with the enterprise architecture, define the boundary, mission, operating environment, roles, information types, categorization, threats, requirements, connections and the baseline with its tailoring, and were developed with the privacy officer, the ISSO, the ISSE, the CSSP and the providers. The AODR approved the plan set with changes on 2026-11-18, but the approval's condition is open: the PM has not approved the contingency, incident response and configuration management plans (due 2026-12-15). The privacy risk assessment result the plans give is the 0.9 draft PIA, not an approved one. The approved plans were distributed to the named roles and are held under document control and role-based access. Interviewed the ISSM. The SSP records pl-2 as partial.

observations.title: ps-4 determination
observations.description: Tested ten leavers drawn from three months of out-processing records, the two of the 2026-10-06 review included, against their EFRAS disable times (the test shared with ac-2). No leaver's checklist records a notification to the account manager, and the two known leavers kept their EFRAS accounts until the quarterly review, so disabling within one working day (same day when involuntary) is not demonstrated for any of them (ASM-020). The rest of the checklist works: all ten show the CAC turned in to the security office, the supervisor's exit briefing with the CUI and PII topics signed, no privileged equipment or keys to retrieve, and the leavers' exports retained in CMP-OBJ for the ISSO and the information owner. Interviewed the ISSO.

observations.title: pt-3 determination
observations.description: Examined the SORN's purpose and routine-use sections (public), the draft PIA and the CCB records that route PII changes to the privacy representative, and every export path and the training extract. Re-performed the re-identification of a sample export with 50 DoD ID numbers drawn from the synthetic population, reusing the red team's PT-2 result (RR-002): the unsalted hash of the DoD ID number joined the export records back to the individuals, as PT-2 found; the design is unchanged until release 1.6. The exports and the training extract may be used only de-identified, so their processing is not restricted to what the purposes allow. The privacy office's metric (zero re-identifiable exports) is not met. Interviewed the privacy officer. The SSP records pt-3 as partial.

observations.title: ra-5 determination
observations.description: Examined a quarter of weekly scan reports, the pipeline gate records of 1.5.0 and 1.5.1, the CSSP's external scan reports and alert tickets, and every remediation ticket since 2026-10-20. Scanning is weekly on nodes and database, on every build for images and dependencies, and monthly at the edge by the CSSP, with SCAP content, CVE and CVSS and daily signature updates; results are analyzed by the ISSM and the engineers and shared with the ISSO, the CSSP and the software factory. Tested with the SCA's own authenticated scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23 (12 hosts, images and database instances): it confirmed the two high vulnerabilities of example-imagelib 2.9.1 in efras-report, found on 2026-10-20, past the 30-day remediation time; release 1.5.2 was not verified (ASM-024). Interviewed the CSSP liaison and the developer lead. The SSP records ra-5 as partial. M-2 2027-02-01 (data to 2026-11-15): still other-than-satisfied. The factory's nightly rescan and the provider's node scan of 2026-11-14 show the two highs in efras-report still open (now 104 days, against 30) and one new medium in the web framework runtime of efras-api (INV-016), first seen on that scan; nodes show no high or critical. The CSSP's alert on the managed Kubernetes version was acted on by the provider (CHG-002). No scan after 2026-11-14 and no CSSP external scan report for the cycle reached the assessor, so whether release 1.6 carries the INV-016 fix is not known. FND-019 stays open; the INV-016 medium is listed for M-3's vulnerability analysis.

observations.title: ra-8 determination
observations.description: Examined the whole draft PIA (version 0.9 of 2026-09-30, ART-PIA) and its coordination record against the system's PII inventory. It covers the five PII elements, the EMIS source and the uses, but it is not approved (privacy office review 2027-01-20, CIO approval 2027-01-25) and has the open item on the de-identified exports; development of EFRAS began before it was drafted. No real maintainer PII has been processed: the pre-production pilot uses synthetic data. EFRAS starts no collection from individuals. Interviewed the privacy officer. The SSP records ra-8 as partial. M-2 2027-02-01: due through POAM-010's milestones; not reassessed, result kept. pia.yaml records the privacy office review of 2027-01-20 and the CIO's approval of 2027-01-25, but both rest on P-14's assumption (ASM-011) and the R-3 progress rule (ASM-025), and no signed PIA is in the run for the assessor to examine; the privacy officer's monitoring record of 2026-11-13 still showed the PIA unapproved. FND-020 stays open.

observations.title: sa-11 determination
observations.description: Examined ERST's test and evaluation plan (security and privacy cases), every pipeline gate of 1.5.0, every DT-2 test card and the flaw tickets (examined, not reused as results, POL-02). Re-performed 12 DT-2 cases on 2026-12-02, drawn at random plus the tampered extract and the API scoping cases: each gave the DT-2 result again. Flaw remediation is verifiable (tickets with severity and due date, closed on a passing retest, as PT-1 on 2026-11-10). Flaws found in testing are not all corrected: the two report container highs are open past their due date and the PT-3 retest has not been done (ASM-022). APR-001 (REQ-11, standards registry) and APR-002 (REQ-12, Section 508): the program holds no standards list checked against the registry and no accessibility test, so neither requirement is demonstrated (ASM-023). Interviewed the developer lead. The SSP records sa-11 as partial.

observations.title: sc-7 determination
observations.description: Examined the templates for the three subnet tiers and their security groups, the WAF rules at CMP-EDGE, the egress allow-list and its change of 2026-11-03, the access point agreement (EXT-002, not tested) and the connection records for EMIS, the supply service and the identity broker. Tested the EFRAS side: ingress reaches only CMP-EDGE on 443 from the access point path, no node has a public address, the tiers pass only the documented ports, and denied traffic is logged in CMP-LOGS; the edge sits alone in its subnet. Reused the first penetration test (RR-002): no unauthenticated access, PT-3 sandbox egress to a public mirror. The allow-list wildcard behind PT-3 is removed in the configuration, but the red team's retest has not shown that the sandbox can no longer reach a public destination (ASM-022), so control of egress at the external interface is not demonstrated. Interviewed the ISSE.

observations.title: si-2 determination
observations.description: Examined the flaw tickets since 2026-10-20, the pipeline gates of 1.5.0 and 1.5.1 that test each fix in pre-production before release, the monthly node image rolls, the change records with ISSO sign-off (cm-3) and the cloud region's October deliverable for the hypervisor, control plane, database engine and host firmware patching it carries (EXT-001, not re-tested; none late). Flaws are identified, reported and tracked, and fixes are tested before installation and installed through configuration management. The SCA's scan of 2026-11-23 confirmed the two high vulnerabilities in example-imagelib 2.9.1 in efras-report not installed within 30 days of the fix's release, because the factory's hardened base image is late; 1.5.2 was not verified (ASM-024). Interviewed the developer lead and the provider's liaison. The SSP records si-2 as partial.

risks.title: Re-identification of maintainers from exports and the training extract
risks.description: Threat: anyone holding an export or the training extract and a list of DoD ID numbers (TE-02). Weakness: the unsalted DoD ID hash used as the join key, and a PIA not approved before development (VUL-01, VUL-07). Effect: maintainers named in data treated as de-identified, beyond the SORN and PIA purposes; harm to about 30,000 individuals.
risks.statement: Likelihood moderate and impact moderate give a moderate risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Exploitation of the unpatched report container
risks.description: Threat: an adversary with a signed-in session sends a crafted rendering request (TE-03). Weakness: two public high vulnerabilities in example-imagelib past the 30-day flaw remediation time, uncorrected developer test findings (VUL-02). Effect: compromise of CMP-REPORT and the reports it renders.
risks.statement: Likelihood moderate and impact moderate give a moderate risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Leavers keep access to readiness data and maintainer records
risks.description: Threat: a departed or transferred maintainer who still holds a CAC, or anyone using that account (TE-09). Weakness: no leaver notification reaches the account manager; only the 35-day inactivity disable and the quarterly review catch it (VUL-10). Effect: unauthorized reading of maintainer PII and readiness data.
risks.statement: Likelihood moderate and impact moderate give a moderate risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Insecure or drifting configuration of the database and application containers
risks.description: Threat: a privileged insider error or an attacker exploiting a weak setting (TE-05, TE-10). Weakness: two open CAT II PostgreSQL STIG settings, no documented secure configuration for the five containers, an inventory not updated at release, and (M-3) a console role that can change security groups outside change control (VUL-09, VUL-11, VUL-13). Effect: an insecure setting or drift goes unnoticed, weakening audit and database account protection.
risks.statement: Likelihood moderate and impact moderate give a moderate risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Regional outage outlasts the recovery objectives
risks.description: Threat: failure of the cloud region or a managed service (TE-06). Weakness: failover never tested, contingency and incident response plans not approved, no exercise or lessons learned (VUL-05). Effect: daily readiness reporting unavailable beyond its objectives.
risks.statement: Likelihood low and impact low give a low risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: EMIS exchange governed by an interim approval only
risks.description: Threat: a tampered extract or a breach at either end with no agreed notification (TE-04). Weakness: no signed memorandum of agreement with security, privacy and breach terms (VUL-03). Effect: integrity and breach handling of maintainer PII rest on goodwill.
risks.statement: Likelihood low and impact moderate give a low risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Break-glass console accounts authenticate without CAC
risks.description: Threat: misuse or error with a break-glass account (TE-05). Weakness: two sealed FIDO2 accounts attributed only through the seal log (VUL-04). Effect: privileged console actions not tied to a proofed identity.
risks.statement: Likelihood low and impact moderate give a low risk level (SP 800-30); response: accept.

risks.title: Training extract leaves through the sandbox's outbound path
risks.description: Threat: a data scientist or a malicious package (TE-08). Weakness: the narrowed NAT allow-list is not retested (VUL-08). Effect: maintainer PII in the training extract leaves the boundary.
risks.statement: Likelihood low and impact moderate give a low risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Incidents older than 90 days cannot be reconstructed from program records
risks.description: Threat: an incident discovered late (TE-07). Weakness: 90-day program audit retention against the one-year requirement (VUL-06). Effect: investigation depends on the CSSP's copy.
risks.statement: Likelihood low and impact low give a low risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

risks.title: Control degradation goes unnoticed before monitoring and recurring assessment start
risks.description: Threat: any of the threat sources acting on a control that degrades unnoticed (TE-11). Weakness: no ongoing assessment or status reporting yet, no recurring assessment scheduled, no POA&M at assessment, plan approval conditional, REQ-11 and REQ-12 not demonstrated (VUL-12). Effect: weaknesses found late.
risks.statement: Likelihood low and impact moderate give a low risk level (SP 800-30); response: mitigate.

findings.title: Departures do not reach the account manager within 24 hours; leaver accounts stay active until the quarterly review
findings.description: AC-2 as tailored requires account managers to be notified within 24 hours when users are terminated or transferred, accounts to be disabled per that policy, and account management aligned with termination and transfer. The 2026-10-06 review found two accounts of users who had left a pilot squadron still active; they were removed at the review, not on departure. The leaver-timing test of ten leavers (2026-12-01) found no notification time for any of them: the out-processing step relies on an e-mail from the squadron office that was not sent for the two known leavers and is not recorded for the others. Evidence: the account review record, the ISSO interview, the out-processing checklists (ASM-020).
findings.remarks: Feed departures and transfers from the squadrons' out-processing into the account manager's queue automatically (or a recorded hand-off with a timestamp), disable the EFRAS account and remove the broker group within 24 hours, and check leaver timing in each quarterly review until production.

findings.title: Audit records are retained 90 days, not the one year the tailored control requires
findings.description: AU-11 as tailored requires audit records retained for one year to support after-the-fact investigations and Component retention requirements. The three log stores hold 90 days; the oldest record each returned on query was 90 days old. The CSSP keeps a one-year copy for its own analysis, retrievable by ticket and under a schedule the program does not control. Evidence: log store retention settings and lifecycle rules, the retrieval test, the ISSO and CSSP interviews, the known limitation (conops item 6).
findings.remarks: Add the archive tier (release 1.6) holding one year of records under the program's control; until then record in the CSSP agreement that the CSSP keeps EFRAS records one year and returns them on request within a set time.

findings.title: No control assessment has yet been completed and reported, and the recurring assessment is not scheduled
findings.description: CA-2 requires controls to be assessed annually (a third each year), an assessment report produced and the results provided to the AO, the PM and the ISSM. The assessor selection and the approved plan are in place (2026-11-18). This first assessment is in progress; no report has yet been produced or delivered, and the annual assessment set is not chosen or scheduled. Evidence: sap.yaml, ART-SAP, ART-CONMON, the ISSM interview. A-5 reassessment: examined sar-report.yaml and ART-SAR on 2026-12-14; the report is produced and was delivered to the PM, the ISSM, the AODR and the AO on 2026-12-11, which meets CA-02e. and CA-02f. for this assessment, but the recurring annual assessment of a third of the controls is still not chosen or scheduled (CA-02d.), so the finding stays open.
findings.remarks: Deliver this assessment's report (A-4) to the AO, the PM and the ISSM, then choose and schedule the first annual third of the controls in the continuous monitoring plan, and update the ca-2 SSP statement to the as-assessed state.

findings.title: The EMIS exchange runs on an interim e-mail approval with no signed agreement
findings.description: CA-3 requires each information exchange to be approved and managed through an agreement documenting interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, controls, responsibilities and the impact level. The nightly EMIS extract, which carries maintainer PII and CUI, runs on the EMIS ISSM's interim e-mail approval of 2026-09-15, which names only the interface; the memorandum of agreement is drafted and under legal review (target 2026-12-31). The two other exchanges have signed agreements. The EFRAS end's mutual TLS and signature check were tested and work. Evidence: the agreements, the interim e-mail, the PM interview, conops limitation 3.
findings.remarks: Sign the EFRAS-EMIS memorandum of agreement with the security and privacy requirements, breach notification, responsibilities of each side and the impact level, before production data flows; record it in boundary.yaml and the SSP.

findings.title: No plan of action and milestones exists for the system
findings.description: CA-5 requires a POA&M documenting planned remediation of weaknesses and known vulnerabilities, updated monthly. The eMASS POA&M module is empty; the seven known limitations are tracked only as backlog tickets with fix releases. Evidence: eMASS, the backlog, the ISSM and PM interviews.
findings.remarks: Create the POA&M at A-6 from this assessment's findings, the open STIG items and the known limitations, with milestones and dates, and update it monthly.

findings.title: Continuous monitoring has not yet run under the approved strategy: no ongoing assessment and no status reporting
findings.description: CA-7 requires system-level continuous monitoring under the strategy, including ongoing control assessments and reporting of the security and privacy status to the AO through the AODR, the PM and the ISSM. The strategy was approved on 2026-11-18 and scanning, log review, drift checks and account reviews run in pre-production, but no ongoing control assessment has run and neither the monthly roll-up nor the quarterly posture report has been produced. Evidence: ART-CONMON, the monitoring records, the ISSM and PM interviews.
findings.remarks: Run the first monitoring cycle after the decision as ART-CONMON sets out, produce the first monthly roll-up and quarterly posture report, and start the annual third of control assessments.

findings.title: Database connection logging verbosity is below the PostgreSQL STIG value (STG-001, CAT II)
findings.description: CM-6 requires the established configuration settings to be implemented. The SCA-witnessed scan of 2026-10-22 and the SCA's scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23 both show the connection logging verbosity on INV-010 below the PostgreSQL STIG value (STG-001, CAT II). The fix is in release 1.5.2 (2026-12-10), which had not reached pre-production by the scan. Evidence: RR-001, the 2026-11-23 scan, stig-summary.yaml, the ISSE and developer interviews.
findings.remarks: Deploy release 1.5.2 with the corrected setting, rescan the database and close STG-001 on the scan result.

findings.title: No secure configuration is established for the five application containers (Application Security and Development STIG not applied)
findings.description: CM-6 requires configuration settings reflecting the most restrictive mode consistent with operations to be established and documented for the components, using the common secure configurations the SSP names. The five application containers (INV-002 to INV-006), which hold and serve the PII and CUI, have no documented settings against the Application Security and Development STIG; the program never completed the checklist (ASM-019), and the assessor's review on 2026-11-24 had nothing to compare the containers against (ASM-021). The pipeline scans and the factory base image cover vulnerabilities and the base layer, not the application settings. Evidence: stig-summary.yaml BM-04, the developer and ISSE interviews.
findings.remarks: Complete the Application Security and Development STIG checklist for each of the five containers, document the resulting settings in the baseline, record open items in stig-summary.yaml, and add a pipeline check for the settings that can be automated.

findings.title: The inventory was not reviewed or updated at release 1.5.1
findings.description: CM-8 as tailored requires the inventory to be reviewed and updated monthly and at every release. Release 1.5.1 reached the assessed environment on 2026-11-07; the inventory still lists the five containers at 1.5.0 and no review at that release is recorded. The monthly review of 2026-11-02 is on file and the inventory is otherwise complete and accurate. Evidence: the INV list, the review records, the ISSE interview.
findings.remarks: Review and update the inventory at each release as the SSP states, and record which release each environment runs, so the inventory matches the release deployed to production.

findings.title: A configuration-controlled change can be made from the provider console without review or approval
findings.description: CM-3 requires proposed configuration-controlled changes to be reviewed and approved or disapproved with explicit consideration of security and privacy impact analyses. On 2026-11-04 a cloud operations engineer widened a security group from the provider console while troubleshooting, outside the pull request, gate and board path and without raising an emergency change; it was neither reviewed nor approved before it was made. The drift scan flagged it within the hour and the pipeline reverted it, so the monitoring part of CM-3 worked, but the engineers' console role can still write security groups in both accounts, and counseling the team does not remove that path. Found in the first ongoing assessment (M-2, 2027-02-01) on the cycle's drift record, which covers pre-production to 2026-11-15. Evidence: product/monitoring/cycle-2026-11.md#drift, CHG-001, the ISSO interview.
findings.remarks: Make the engineers' console role read-only for network and security group settings in both accounts, keep a break-glass path that raises an emergency change and pages the ISSO, and show the change on the next drift record and access review.

findings.title: The contingency plan is a draft: not reviewed or approved by the PM, not distributed, not under review
findings.description: CP-2 as tailored requires the contingency plan to be reviewed and approved by the PM, distributed to the on-call engineers, the ISSO, the ISSM, EMIS and the CSSP, reviewed annually and its changes communicated to them. The version 1.0 draft covers the content the control requires, but has no review or approval, has gone to nobody outside the program repository, and no review or change communication has happened. Evidence: ART-CP, the repository, the ISSE interview; the S-6 approval sets a PM approval date of 2026-12-15.
findings.remarks: Have the PM review and approve the plan by 2026-12-15, distribute it to the named personnel and to EMIS and the CSSP, and record the annual review date.

findings.title: Regional failover has never been tested and no tabletop exercise has been held
findings.description: CP-4 as tailored requires the contingency plan to be tested annually with a tabletop exercise, a database restore test and a regional failover test. Only the database restore has been tested (DT-2, re-performed by the assessor on 2026-12-02, within objective). The regional failover of the cluster, on which recovery from a regional outage depends, and the tabletop exercise have never been held; both are planned for 2027-02, after the planned deployment of 2027-02-01. Evidence: test records, the restore re-performance, the ISSE interview, conops limitation 4.
findings.remarks: Hold the tabletop and the regional failover test before production use if the schedule allows, otherwise as early in 2027-02 as possible, review the results and record corrective actions in the plan and the POA&M.

findings.title: Two break-glass console accounts authenticate with FIDO2 keys instead of CAC, and the deviation is not accepted
findings.description: IA-2 requires organizational users to be uniquely identified and authenticated, which DoD meets with CAC (PKI). The two break-glass cloud console accounts use FIDO2 hardware keys because the console cannot federate when the identity broker is down; each use is tied to a person only through the two-person seal log and the alert, not by the credential. The keys are sealed and unused; the deviation has not been recorded or accepted by the AO. Evidence: the account list, the seal log, the ISSO interview, conops limitation 5.
findings.remarks: Record the deviation with its compensating measures (sealed keys, two-person opening, alerting, post-use review) for the AO's acceptance, and review each break-glass use against the seal log within one working day.

findings.title: The local break-glass database role's password complexity falls short of the PostgreSQL STIG (STG-002, CAT II)
findings.description: IA-5 requires authenticators to have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use. The password of the local break-glass database role on INV-010 does not meet the PostgreSQL STIG complexity rule (STG-002, CAT II) on the 2026-10-22 scan and on the SCA's scan of release 1.5.1 on 2026-11-23. The password is sealed, changed within 180 days and its role unused. The fix is in release 1.5.2 (2026-12-10), not yet in pre-production. Evidence: both scans, stig-summary.yaml, the ISSO and ISSE interviews.
findings.remarks: Deploy release 1.5.2 with the database password policy the STIG requires, reset the break-glass password under it, rescan and close STG-002.

findings.title: Incident handling is not tied to an approved plan, not coordinated with an approved contingency plan, and has no lessons-learned step in operation
findings.description: IR-4 requires an incident handling capability consistent with the incident response plan, coordinated with contingency planning, with lessons learned incorporated into procedures, training and testing. The CSSP's detection and analysis and the program's containment, eradication and recovery runbooks are in place, but the incident response plan is an unapproved draft nobody has been trained on, the contingency plan it coordinates with is also an unapproved draft, and no incident, exercise or after-action review has taken place. Evidence: ART-IRP, the runbook, the ISSO and CSSP interviews, conops limitation 4.
findings.remarks: Approve ART-IRP and ART-CP by 2026-12-15, train the plan's holders on them, and hold the combined incident and contingency tabletop (planned 2027-02) with an after-action report that feeds the runbooks, training and the next exercise.

findings.title: The incident response plan is a draft: not approved, not distributed, no change communicated
findings.description: IR-8 as specified requires the plan to be reviewed and approved by the PM with the ISSM's review and the CISO office's concurrence, distributed to the ISSO, the ISSM, the on-call engineers, the CSSP and the privacy office, and its changes communicated to them. ART-IRP covers the content the control requires but has no review or approval and has reached nobody outside the program repository. Evidence: ART-IRP, incident-response.yaml, the ISSM interview; approval is due 2026-12-15.
findings.remarks: Have the PM approve the plan by 2026-12-15 after the ISSM's review and the CISO office's concurrence, distribute it to the named personnel and organizations, and record the annual review date.

findings.title: The plan set's approval condition is open and its privacy risk assessment result is a draft PIA
findings.description: PL-2 requires security and privacy plans that give the results of a privacy risk assessment and are reviewed and approved by the AO or designated representative before implementation. The AODR approved the plan set on 2026-11-18 on the condition that the PM approves the contingency, incident response and configuration management plans by 2026-12-15; none is approved yet (see FND-010 and FND-015). The privacy risk assessment the plans rely on is the 0.9 draft PIA, still with the Component privacy office (see FND-020). Evidence: the approval record, ART-SSP, ART-PIA, the ISSM interview.
findings.remarks: Have the PM approve the three plans by 2026-12-15 and record that the AODR's condition is met; replace the draft PIA reference with the approved PIA when the CIO approves it (planned 2027-01-25).

findings.title: Leavers' EFRAS access is not disabled within the set time; it waits for the inactivity disable or the quarterly review
findings.description: PS-4 as specified requires system access to be disabled within one working day of a voluntary departure and the same day for an involuntary one. The leaver-timing test of ten leavers (2026-12-01) found no notification to the EFRAS account manager on any checklist, and the two leavers found at the 2026-10-06 review were still active when they were removed there. The same evidence is FND-001 under ac-2; this finding records the personnel security side, which the out-processing checklist owns. Evidence: the checklists, the account review record, the ISSO interviews (ASM-020).
findings.remarks: Add a recorded, timestamped step to the squadrons' out-processing checklist that reaches the EFRAS account manager (or an automatic feed), disable the account within the set time, and sample leaver timing at each quarterly review; remediate together with FND-001.

findings.title: De-identified exports and the training extract are re-identifiable through an unsalted DoD ID hash
findings.description: PT-3 as specified restricts processing to what the purposes allow: analysts' exports and the data scientists' training extract only de-identified. Both keep a stable, unsalted hash of the DoD ID number as the join key. The red team re-identified records with 50 DoD ID numbers (PT-2), and the assessor's re-performance on 2026-12-07 did the same. Anyone with a list of ID numbers can re-identify maintainers in an export. Evidence: the export pipeline, the re-identification test, conops limitation 1, the privacy officer's interview.
findings.remarks: Ship salted, rotated pseudonyms in release 1.6 (2027-01-15) and retest re-identification before production. Until then, restrict exports and the training extract to the analysts and data scientists who need them and keep the PIA's open item with the privacy office.

findings.title: Two high vulnerabilities in the report container are past the 30-day remediation time
findings.description: RA-5 as specified requires critical and high vulnerabilities to be remediated within 30 days of discovery. The dependency and image scans of 2026-10-20 found two high vulnerabilities in example-imagelib 2.9.1 inside efras-report (CMP-REPORT); the due date of 2026-11-19 passed and the SCA's scan of 2026-11-23 confirmed both. The fix waits on the software factory's hardened base image; release 1.5.2 (planned 2026-12-10) was not verified during the assessment. Evidence: pipeline records, the SCA scan, remediation tickets, the developer's interview, conops limitation 2.
findings.remarks: Deploy release 1.5.2 with the hardened base image as soon as the factory delivers it and rescan; if the base image slips again, ask the factory for an interim image or isolate the report renderer further, and record the risk decision.

findings.title: No approved privacy impact assessment; development began before the PIA was drafted
findings.description: RA-8 requires a privacy impact assessment before developing information technology that processes PII. EFRAS was developed before the PIA was drafted, and the PIA is still the 0.9 draft with the privacy office, with an open item on the de-identified exports (FND-018). Approval is planned for 2027-01-25, before production data flows. Evidence: ART-PIA, the coordination record, the privacy officer's interview.
findings.remarks: Resolve the export item (release 1.6), complete the privacy office review on 2027-01-20 and obtain the CIO's approval before any production data flows; hold production ingest until then.

findings.title: Flaws found in developer and penetration testing are not all corrected: the report container highs and the PT-3 retest
findings.description: SA-11 requires the developer to correct flaws identified during testing and evaluation. The two high vulnerabilities found in the efras-report image on 2026-10-20 are not corrected (release 1.5.2 not verified, FND-019), and PT-3, the sandbox egress to a public mirror, was narrowed on 2026-11-03 but has not been retested, so its correction is not verified (ASM-022). PT-1 shows the remediation process works when the fix is in the program's hands. Evidence: pipeline records, the flaw tickets, the penetration test report, the developer's interview.
findings.remarks: Close both flaws on a passing retest: rescan efras-report after release 1.5.2 and have the red team retest the sandbox egress, then close the tickets.

findings.title: REQ-11 (DoD IT Standards Registry) and REQ-12 (Section 508) are not verified
findings.description: S-3 allocated REQ-11 and REQ-12 to sa-11 as developer verification, and the plan added APR-001 and APR-002 to verify them. On 2026-12-03 the program had no list of the protocols and standards on the access point, identity broker, EMIS and CSSP interfaces checked against the DoD IT Standards Registry, and no Section 508 conformance check or assistive technology test of the five role workflows. Neither requirement can be shown met; no particular nonconformance was found either (ASM-023). Evidence: the test and evaluation plan, the DT-2 report, the developer's interview.
findings.remarks: Add a standards registry review of each interface and a Section 508 conformance check with assistive technology to the next DT event before the authorization decision, and record both results against REQ-11 and REQ-12.

findings.title: The fix for the sandbox egress to a public mirror (PT-3) has not been retested
findings.description: SC-7 requires communications at external managed interfaces to be controlled; the plan allows sandbox egress only to the listed endpoints. The first penetration test downloaded packages from a public mirror through the NAT allow-list wildcard (PT-3, low). The wildcard was removed on 2026-11-03, but the retest the plan scheduled in the second penetration test has no result, so the closure is not demonstrated. Evidence: the allow-list change, the penetration test report, the ISSE's interview (ASM-022).
findings.remarks: Have the red team retest egress from CMP-SANDBOX against public destinations and close PT-3 on a passing result; add a periodic automated egress probe from the sandbox.

findings.title: Security-relevant updates for the report container are not installed within 30 days
findings.description: SI-2 as specified requires security-relevant software updates to be installed within 30 days of their release. The upstream fix for the two high vulnerabilities in example-imagelib 2.9.1 inside efras-report is released, but EFRAS may build only from the software factory's hardened base image, and the one carrying the fix is late; the SCA's scan of 2026-11-23 confirmed the vulnerable library in place, and release 1.5.2 (planned 2026-12-10) was not verified. Evidence: tickets, the SCA scan, the developer's interview, conops limitation 2. Same root cause as FND-019 (ra-5).
findings.remarks: Install the fix through release 1.5.2 as soon as the factory's base image is available and rescan; agree with the factory an interim path (such as a patched intermediate image) for when its base image is late, and track that dependency with its POA&M item.
